title: 白马篇
author: 曹植
note: 【酒】酒，古典诗词中常用于遣怀、送别、消愁。
【白马篇】汉魏六朝代曹植所作的诗。
tr: 龍馬花雪毛，金鞍五陵豪。秋霜切玉劒，落日明珠袍。鬬雞事萬乘，軒蓋一何高。弓摧南山虎，手接太行猱。酒後競風采，三杯弄寶刀。殺人如剪草，劇孟同遊遨。發憤去函谷，從軍向臨洮。叱咤萬戰場，匈奴盡奔逃。歸來使酒氣，未肯拜蕭曹。羞入原憲室，荒淫隱蓬蒿。
appr: 《白马篇》是汉魏六朝代曹植所作的诗名篇。作品采用四言为主的句式，古朴厚重，直陈其事，是先秦古诗典型风格。艺术上，作品善于选取典型意象融情于景，用词精炼传神，于平淡处见深情，读来余韵悠长。作为汉魏六朝代诗歌的经典篇章，《白马篇》历代传诵不衰，是曹植诗歌风格的集中体现。

en_body: The dragon steed bears a coat like snow-kissed blooms,
Gold saddle adorns the gallant of the Five Tombs.
Keen as autumn frost his jade-cutting sword gleams,
Setting sun gilds the pearls embroidered on his robe.
He served the Son of Heaven through cockfighting fame,
How lofty his carriage canopy towers above all!
His bow lays low the fierce tigers of South Mountain,
Barehanded he catches the swift gibbons of Taihang.
After wine they vie to show their gallant spirit,
Three cups down, they flourish their precious blades.
Slaying foes is as easy as trimming grass,
They roam with knight-errants like Ju Meng at their side.
Stirred by resolve, they march toward Hangu Pass,
Joining the army, they ride for Lintao's frontier.
With a battle cry they charge through a thousand fields,
The Xiongnu invaders turn and flee in utter terror.
Back from war they give themselves to wine and pride,
Refusing to bow to ministers like Xiao and Cao.
Ashamed to dwell in Yuan Xian's narrow humble hut,
They live free and wild, hidden among the reeds.

baihua_lines: 那匹骏马浑身雪白，鬃毛像覆盖着雪花。
配着金鞍，骑乘的是五陵的豪杰少年。
腰间宝剑锋利如秋霜，能切削美玉。
夕阳映照下，锦袍上的明珠闪闪发光。
曾因斗鸡得到帝王的赏识与宠幸。
出门时车马华盖，排场景况何等气派。
弯弓就能射杀南山猛虎，膂力惊人。
徒手便能接住太行山上敏捷的猿猱。
酒酣之后众人争强好胜，尽显风采。
三杯下肚便舞弄宝刀，意气风发。
铲除恶人如同割草一般干脆利落。
与剧孟那样的侠义之士交游行侠。
满怀报国壮志，奔赴函谷关从军。
随军出征，直奔临洮前线御敌。
在万千战场上叱咤风云，威震敌胆。
杀得匈奴兵马丢盔弃甲，四散奔逃。
战功归来仍纵情使酒，豪气不减。
不肯屈身拜谒萧何、曹参那样的权贵。
耻于像原宪那样安于贫贱、困守陋室。
宁愿放浪形骸，自在隐于草莽之间。

title: 红楼梦·好了歌注
author: 曹雪芹
body: 乱烘烘你方唱罢我登场，
到头来都是为他人作嫁衣裳！
note: 【故乡】家乡、故土，寄托归思之情。
【红楼梦·好了歌注】明清代曹雪芹所作的诗。
tr: 陋室空堂，当年笏满床；衰草枯杨，曾为歌舞场。蛛丝儿结满雕梁，绿纱今又糊在蓬窗上。说什么脂正浓，粉正香，如何两鬓又成霜？昨日黄土陇头送白骨，今宵红灯帐底卧鸳鸯。金满箱，银满箱，转眼乞丐人皆谤。正叹他人命不长，那知自己归来丧！训有方，保不定日后作强梁。择膏粱，谁承望流落在烟花巷！因嫌纱帽小，致使锁枷扛。昨怜破袄寒，今嫌紫蟒长。乱烘烘你方唱罢我登场，反认他乡是故乡。甚荒唐，到头来都是为他人作嫁衣裳！

en_body: Mean hovels and empty halls, once grand and tall,
Where tablets of office once piled high on beds; now withered grass and dying willows stand
These grounds once echoed with song and dance.
Cobwebs hang thick across the carved beams,
Green gauze now pasted on the cottage windows.
Talk not of rouge applied so rich and deep,
Of fragrant powder, sweet and fresh to see—
How is it that both temples have turned to frost?
Yesterday by yellow mounds they buried white bones,
Tonight beneath red lanterns love-birds lie.
Gold crammed in chests,
Silver piled high in coffers and in trays—
In a blink, a beggar scorned by all who pass.
Sighing that others' lives are all too brief,
Who knows that you yourself will soon return to die!
Train your sons with all the care you may,
None can ensure they will not turn to banditry.
Choose a son-in-law from the noblest rich,
Who dreams your daughter ends up in the brothels!
Grumbling that your official hat's too small,
You end up locked in cangue and iron chains.
Yesterday you pitied rags against the cold,
Today you grumble your purple robe's too long.
All confusion: you exit, I come on stage,
Mistaking a strange land for your native home.
How absurd it all becomes at last—
You have but sewn the wedding gown for someone else!

en_title: Honglou Meng: Note to the Song of Good and Done
lines: 乱烘烘你方唱罢我登场，
到头来都是为他人作嫁衣裳！
baihua_lines: 那简陋空荡的堂屋，
当年笏板曾堆满床；如今枯草衰杨，
这里曾是歌舞升平的场所。
雕花的梁上结满了蛛网，
绿纱如今又糊在了茅草窗上。
说什么胭脂正浓，
香粉芬芳，
怎么两鬓转眼就成了白霜？
昨日还在黄土坡前埋葬白骨，
今夜红灯帐底便已鸳鸯成双。
黄金装满箱，
白银堆满柜，
转眼沦为乞丐，人人争相毁谤。
正叹息他人寿命不长，
哪知自己归来便一命身亡！
教导儿子有方，
保不定日后他去做强梁。
挑选富贵子弟为婿，
谁料想女儿竟流落烟花巷！
只因嫌官职太小，
最终落得枷锁扛身。
昨日还怜破袄寒冷，
今日便嫌紫蟒太长。
乱哄哄你刚唱罢我又登场，
反倒把他乡认作了故乡。
多么荒唐啊，
到头来都是为别人做嫁衣裳！

en_lines: Mean hovels and empty halls, once grand and tall,
Where tablets of office once piled high on beds; now withered grass and dying willows stand
These grounds once echoed with song and dance.
Cobwebs hang thick across the carved beams,
Green gauze now pasted on the cottage windows.
Talk not of rouge applied so rich and deep,
Of fragrant powder, sweet and fresh to see—
How is it that both temples have turned to frost?
Yesterday by yellow mounds they buried white bones,
Tonight beneath red lanterns love-birds lie.
Gold crammed in chests,
Silver piled high in coffers and in trays—
In a blink, a beggar scorned by all who pass.
Sighing that others' lives are all too brief,
Who knows that you yourself will soon return to die!
Train your sons with all the care you may,
None can ensure they will not turn to banditry.
Choose a son-in-law from the noblest rich,
Who dreams your daughter ends up in the brothels!
Grumbling that your official hat's too small,
You end up locked in cangue and iron chains.
Yesterday you pitied rags against the cold,
Today you grumble your purple robe's too long.
All confusion: you exit, I come on stage,
Mistaking a strange land for your native home.
How absurd it all becomes at last—
You have but sewn the wedding gown for someone else!

title: 红楼梦·葬花吟
author: 曹雪芹
body: 却不道人去梁空巢也倾。
note: 【红楼梦·葬花吟】明清代曹雪芹所作的诗。
tr: 花谢花飞花满天，红消香断有谁怜？游丝软系飘春榭，落絮轻沾扑绣帘。闺中女儿惜春暮，愁绪满怀无释处。手把花锄出绣帘，忍踏落花来复去。柳丝榆荚自芳菲，不管桃飘与李飞。桃李明年能再发，明年闺中知有谁？三月香巢已垒成，梁间燕子太无情！明年花发虽可啄，却不道人去梁空巢也倾。一年三百六十日，风刀霜剑严相逼。明媚鲜妍能几时，一朝漂泊难寻觅。花开易见落难寻，阶前闷杀葬花人。独倚花锄泪暗洒，洒上空枝见血痕。杜鹃无语正黄昏，荷锄归去掩重门。青灯照壁人初睡，冷雨敲窗被未温。怪奴底事倍伤神？半为怜春半恼春。怜春忽至恼忽去，至又无言去未闻。昨宵庭外悲歌发，知是花魂与鸟魂？花魂鸟魂总难留，鸟自无言花自羞。愿奴胁下生双翼，随花飞到天尽头。天尽头，何处有香丘？未若锦囊收艳骨，一抔净土掩风流。质本洁来还洁去，强于污淖陷渠沟。尔今死去侬收葬，未卜侬身何日丧？侬今葬花人笑痴，他年葬侬知是谁？试看春残花渐落，便是红颜老死时。一朝春尽红颜老，花落人亡两不知！
appr: 《红楼梦·葬花吟》是明清代曹雪芹所作的诗名篇。全诗共52句，章法舒展，语言自然，情真意切。艺术上，作品善于选取典型意象融情于景，用词精炼传神，于平淡处见深情，读来余韵悠长。作为明清代诗歌的经典篇章，《红楼梦·葬花吟》历代传诵不衰，是曹雪芹诗歌风格的集中体现。

theme: 《红楼梦·葬花吟》主旨在于抒写羁旅思乡之情，表达对故土亲人的深切思念。；写闺阁情思，抒发女子的思念与幽怨。作品以凝练的语言、鲜明的意象，将情感寄寓于景物与叙事之中，含蓄深沉，意蕴丰厚，千百年来引发读者广泛共鸣，是明清代曹雪芹的代表性作品之一。
en_body: Blossoms fade and fly across the sky,
Red fades, scent fails—who will pity them now?
Gossamer drifts soft around the spring pavilion,
Falling catkins brush against the embroidered curtain.
The maiden in her chamber grieves spring's waning,
Her heart brimful of sorrow with no relief.
Taking her flower hoe, she steps beyond the screen,
Unwilling to tread on fallen petals as she comes and goes.
Willow threads and elm seeds flaunt their fragrance,
Heedless of peach and plum blossoms drifting by.
Peach and plum will bloom again when comes next year,
But who will remain within this maiden's bower then?
By third moon the fragrant nest is fully built,
How heartless are the swallows beneath the eaves!
Next year when flowers bloom, again they may peck buds,
Not knowing she'll be gone, the beams bare, the nest o'erthrown.
Three hundred and sixty days each passing year,
Wind like a knife, frost like a sword press cruelly on.
Bright bloom and tender beauty last how long?
Once blown adrift, they are too hard to find again.
Blooms in full sight are easy; fallen, hard to seek—
Before the steps, the flower-burier's heart aches sore.
Leaning alone on her hoe, she sheds secret tears,
Which drop on empty boughs like stains of crimson blood.
The cuckoo falls silent as dusk descends,
Shouldering her hoe, she goes home, closing the gates.
The green lamp lights the wall as sleep first comes,
Cold rain taps the window, the quilt not yet warm.
Ask not why I am so weighed down with grief—
Half pity for spring, half resentment of spring.
I love its swift coming, hate its sudden going,
It comes without a word, leaves without a sound.
Last night beyond the courtyard a sad song rose—
Was that the soul of flowers, or the soul of birds?
Flower souls and bird souls are hard ever to keep,
The bird falls silent; the flower bows its head in shame.
Oh that I might grow wings beneath my arms,
And fly with the flowers to the very edge of heaven!
At heaven's edge,
Where lies the fragrant mound?
Better to wrap these fair bones in a silk pouch,
And cover all this grace with pure clean earth.
Pure you came, and pure you shall return,
Far better than sinking defiled into the mire.
Now you have perished, and I have buried you—
I cannot tell what day I too shall die.
They laugh at my folly, burying flowers today,
Who will it be that buries me in years to come?
See: as spring fades, the blossoms gently fall,
That is the hour when beauty fades and dies.
One day spring will be gone, and youth grown old—
Flowers fallen, the maiden dead, neither will know!

en_title: Honglou Meng: Elegy for Fallen Flowers
lines: 却不道人去梁空巢也倾。
baihua_lines: 花儿凋谢、花瓣纷飞，飘满天空，
红颜褪尽、香气消散，有谁来怜惜？
柔软的游丝轻轻飘在春日的台榭上，
飘落的柳絮轻沾着扑向绣花的帘幕。
闺中少女惋惜着春天即将逝去，
满怀愁绪，找不到可以排遣的地方。
手里拿着花锄，走出绣房的帘子，
怎忍心踩着飘落的花瓣走来走去。
柳丝和榆荚自顾自地吐露着芬芳，
全然不管桃花飘零、李花纷飞。
桃花李花明年还能再度开放，
明年这闺房之中，还会有谁在呢？
三月里燕子的香巢已经垒好了，
梁上的燕子啊，真是太无情了！
明年花开时你们还可以来啄花衔泥，
却想不到人已离去、梁空巢倾。
一年三百六十多天，
寒风如刀、严霜似剑，苦苦相逼。
明媚鲜艳的光景能持续多久呢，
一旦漂泊零落，就再也难以寻觅。
花开时容易看见，落了就难找寻，
台阶前愁坏了葬花的人。
独自倚着花锄，暗暗地洒下泪水，
泪洒在空枝上，仿佛留下了血痕。
黄昏里杜鹃鸟默默无语，
扛着锄头回去，关上了重重院门。
青灯照着墙壁，人刚刚睡下，
冷雨敲打着窗户，被子还没暖热。
别怪我为什么事如此伤神，
一半是因为怜春，一半是因为恼春。
怜它忽然到来，恼它又匆匆离去，
来时悄然无言，去时也无从听闻。
昨夜院子外传来悲切的歌声，
不知是花的魂魄，还是鸟的魂魄？
花魂与鸟魂终究难以挽留，
鸟儿默默无言，花儿也暗自含羞。
但愿我肋下能生出一双翅膀，
跟着花儿飞到天的尽头。
天的尽头啊，
哪里才有埋葬香花的坟丘？
不如用锦袋收起你娇艳的尸骨，
用一抔干净的黄土掩埋这绝代风流。
你本是洁净而来，还是洁净地去吧，
总比陷落在污泥浊水沟里要强。
你如今死去，有我来收葬你，
我不知道自己哪天也会死去？
我今天葬花，别人笑我痴傻，
以后埋葬我的，又会是谁呢？
你看春天将尽，花儿渐渐凋落，
那正是红颜少女衰老死去的时候。
一旦春天过完、红颜老去，
花落了、人死了，两边都茫然不知！

Not knowing she'll be gone, the beams bare, the nest o'erthrown.
Three hundred and sixty days each passing year,
Wind like a knife, frost like a sword press cruelly on.
Bright bloom and tender beauty last how long?
Once blown adrift, they are too hard to find again.
Blooms in full sight are easy; fallen, hard to seek—
Before the steps, the flower-burier's heart aches sore.
Leaning alone on her hoe, she sheds secret tears,
Which drop on empty boughs like stains of crimson blood.
The cuckoo falls silent as dusk descends,
Shouldering her hoe, she goes home, closing the gates.
The green lamp lights the wall as sleep first comes,
Cold rain taps the window, the quilt not yet warm.
Ask not why I am so weighed down with grief—
Half pity for spring, half resentment of spring.
I love its swift coming, hate its sudden going,
It comes without a word, leaves without a sound.
Last night beyond the courtyard a sad song rose—
Was that the soul of flowers, or the soul of birds?
Flower souls and bird souls are hard ever to keep,
The bird falls silent; the flower bows its head in shame.
Oh that I might grow wings beneath my arms,
And fly with the flowers to the very edge of heaven!
At heaven's edge,
Where lies the fragrant mound?
Better to wrap these fair bones in a silk pouch,
And cover all this grace with pure clean earth.
Pure you came, and pure you shall return,
Far better than sinking defiled into the mire.
Now you have perished, and I have buried you—
I cannot tell what day I too shall die.
They laugh at my folly, burying flowers today,
Who will it be that buries me in years to come?
See: as spring fades, the blossoms gently fall,
That is the hour when beauty fades and dies.
One day spring will be gone, and youth grown old—
Flowers fallen, the maiden dead, neither will know!

en_body: Beneath cassia mist and wutong shade we raise our cups,
All Chang'an's mouths water, waiting the Double Ninth.
It crawls ahead, no care for east or west, north or south,
Inside its shell, nothing but black roe and yellow fat.
Wine cannot quell its fishy tang—chrysanthemum we add,
To ward off cold, we must serve it up with ginger.
What use its cunning now, fallen into the pot?
By moonlit banks, only the scent of grain remains.

baihua_lines: 桂花香雾里、梧桐树荫下，坐着举杯饮酒，
长安城里馋嘴的人们都盼着重阳节到来。
螃蟹横爬，眼前的道路不分东西南北，
壳里只有黑膏和蟹黄，空藏着满腹心机。

螃蟹性寒防积冷，吃时一定要配生姜。
如今掉进锅里被烹煮，又有什么用呢，
月光下的水岸边，只剩下禾黍的清香。

author: 曹雪芹
note: 【红楼梦·题帕三绝】明清代曹雪芹所作的诗。

en_body: Eyes brim with tears in vain; tears fall in vain,
Secretly shed, freely scattered—for whom do they fall?
This small square of mermaid silk, so kindly given,
How can it not fill the heart with piercing grief!
Pearls of tears roll down, shed only when none see,
All day no heart for aught, all day idle and still.
On pillow and sleeve the stains are hard to wipe away—
Let them remain, spot after spot, streak upon streak.
Colored threads cannot string the pearls upon the face,
The ancient tear-stains by Xiang River have faded now.
Before my window, too, a thousand bamboo stems grow—
I wonder if my fragrant tears have marked them yet?

baihua_lines: 眼里空自含着泪水，泪水空自垂落，
这样暗暗抛洒，到底是为了谁呢？
劳你相赠这一尺见方的鲛绡手帕，
叫人心里怎么能不悲伤啊！
泪珠像抛珠滚玉一般，只能偷偷落下，
整天没有心思，整天都百无聊赖。
枕头上、袖边的泪痕难以擦拭干净，
就任凭它点点斑斑地留着吧。
彩线也串不起脸上滚落的泪珠，
湘江边娥皇女英的旧泪痕已经模糊。
我的窗前也有上千竿的翠竹，
不知它们可曾被我的泪痕染上斑痕？

en_body: Withered willows line the bay at Baimen Gate,
The tide beats the city wall, then turns again.
Little Chang'an Lane runs into Great Chang'an Lane,
Song clappers and wine flags have all fallen to ruin,
Nothing remains but a few idle fishing rods.
Autumn grass breathes the cold of six dynasties past,
Flower-rain falls on the empty, silent terrace.
Where no soul comes, I lean alone against the rail,
Swallows come and go in the slanting evening sun,
Such is the rivers and mountains!

en_translation: Withered willows line the bay at Baimen Gate,
The tide beats the city wall, then turns again.
Little Chang'an Lane runs into Great Chang'an Lane,
Song clappers and wine flags have all fallen to ruin,
Nothing remains but a few idle fishing rods.
Autumn grass breathes the cold of six dynasties past,
Flower-rain falls on the empty, silent terrace.
Where no soul comes, I lean alone against the rail,
Swallows come and go in the slanting evening sun,
Such is the rivers and mountains!
baihua_lines: 白门湾边的柳树已经衰枯，
江潮拍打着城墙，又退了回去。
小长干街巷连接着大长干。
歌板酒旗都已零落殆尽，
只剩下几根钓鱼的渔竿。
秋草荒寒，带着六朝的萧瑟，
落花如雨，洒在空荡的高台。
在空无一人的地方独自倚栏，
燕子在斜阳里飞来又飞去，
就是这样的大好江山啊！

title: 桂殿秋
author: 朱彝尊
note: 《桂殿秋》是朱彝尊的经典作品，语言凝练，意境深远，为历代读者所传诵。【桂殿秋】明清代朱彝尊所作的诗。
tr: 秋色里，月明中。红旌翠节下蓬宫。蟠桃已结瑶池露，桂子初开玉殿风。

Beneath the bright and shining moon.
Red banners and green staffs descend to the fairy palace,
Peaches of immortality bear dew from Jasper Pool,
Osmanthus first opens as wind stirs the jade hall.

en_body: Feather fan and silk cap, the breeze swaying soft,
East-chamber moonlight reaches the rose-briars.
Who calls new melodies forth from the silken curtains?
Dragon-beard mat wraps the flute in winding tones,
Wild-geese notes fly from the zither into the air.
Middle age needs such things to soothe the heart,
Lingering by moon-fans and cloud-like robes.
Since Zhou Yu passed, true connoisseurs are few.
For you I raise my cup and listen close,
How could I bear to let spring slip away?

baihua_lines: 手持羽扇、头戴纶巾，微风轻柔，
东厢的月光照到了蔷薇花上。

人到中年需要用这些来陶冶性情，
在月扇云衣间流连忘返。
周郎离去之后，知音就稀少了。
为你举杯把酒聆听，
哪里肯让春天就此归去。

title: 出郊
author: 杨慎

tr: 難得晴如許，春游第一番。鳥啼花底樹，雲裹面前山。馬躍平沙地，帆投落日村。戲呼漁子問，吾與汝誰閑。

en_body: Rare indeed is such clear and lovely weather,
The very first spring outing of the year.
Birds sing in the trees beneath the blossoms,
White clouds wrap around the hills ahead.
Horses gambol across the level sandy ground,
Sails head for villages lit by setting sun.
Playfully I call to the fisherman and ask:
Between you and me, who lives the more at leisure?

en_lines: Rare indeed is such clear and lovely weather,
The very first spring outing of the year.
Birds sing in the trees beneath the blossoms,
White clouds wrap around the hills ahead.
Horses gambol across the level sandy ground,
Sails head for villages lit by setting sun.
Playfully I call to the fisherman and ask:
Between you and me, who lives the more at leisure?

title: 少年中国说
author: 梁启超
body: 少年富则国富；少年强则国强，
少年独立则国独立；少年自由则国自由；少年进步则国进步；少年胜于欧洲，
则国胜于欧洲；少年雄于地球，
note: 《少年中国说》是梁启超的经典作品，语言凝练，意境深远，为历代读者所传诵。【少年中国说】明清代梁启超所作的诗。
tr: 故今日之责任，不在他人，而全在我少年。少年智则国智，少年富则国富；少年强则国强，少年独立则国独立；少年自由则国自由；少年进步则国进步；少年胜于欧洲，则国胜于欧洲；少年雄于地球，则国雄于地球。红日初升，其道大光。河出伏流，一泻汪洋。潜龙腾渊，鳞爪飞扬。乳虎啸谷，百兽震惶。鹰隼试翼，风尘翕张。奇花初胎，矞矞皇皇。干将发硎，有作其芒。天戴其苍，地履其黄。纵有千古，横有八荒。前途似海，来日方长。美啊我少年中国，与天不老！壮啊我中国少年，与国无疆！

theme: 《少年中国说》主旨在于登临怀古，借古抒怀，寄寓历史兴亡之感。；抒发爱国情怀与报国之志。作品以凝练的语言、鲜明的意象，将情感寄寓于景物与叙事之中，含蓄深沉，意蕴丰厚，千百年来引发读者广泛共鸣，是明清代梁启超的代表性作品之一。
en_body: Therefore the responsibility of today,
Rests not with others,
But falls entirely upon us youth.
If the youth are wise, the nation will be wise;
If the youth are wealthy, the nation will be wealthy; if the youth are strong, the nation will be strong;
If the youth are independent, the nation will be independent; if the youth are free, the nation will be free; if the youth progress, the nation will progress; if the youth surpass Europe,
The nation will surpass Europe; if the youth dominate the earth,
The nation will dominate the earth.
The red sun is just rising,
Its path streaming with brilliant light.
The Yellow River emerges from underground,
And rushes forth in a mighty flood.
The hidden dragon leaps from the deep abyss,
Its scales and claws flying high in the air.
The tiger cub roars in the valley,
And a hundred beasts tremble in terror.
Eagles and falcons test their wings for flight,
As wind and dust billow upward high.
Rare flowers begin to form their buds,
Splendid, glorious, full of life.
The Ganjiang sword is newly drawn from the whetstone,
Its edge shines with a dazzling brilliance.
Above us we wear the blue of heaven,
Beneath our feet we tread the yellow earth.
Stretching back through a thousand ancient years,
Reaching out to the eight wilds in every direction.
The future lies before us like a sea,
And the days ahead are long indeed.
How beautiful is our Young China,
As ageless as the very heavens above!
How magnificent our Chinese youth,
Boundless as the motherland, eternal and strong!

body: 古今之成大事业、大学问者，

note: 【天涯】天的尽头，指极远之地，常与漂泊、相思相连。

en_body: Throughout all time, those who achieve great things or master great learning,
Must of necessity pass through three stages: last night the west wind stripped the green trees bare,
Alone I climbed the lofty tower,
And gazed to the very end of the long road to the horizon.
This marks the first stage.
My girdle grows loose and loose, yet never do I regret,
For her sake I willingly grow pale and gaunt with longing.
This marks the second stage.
A thousand times I searched for her among the crowd,
When suddenly I turned my head,
And there she stood,
Where the lantern light is dimmest and most faint.
This marks the third stage.

en_body: Spring waters rise a pole's depth, widening the surface of the pond.
Among sweet-scented grass, goslings paddle at play,
The breeze-kissed banks are clothed in green.
Painted boats drift slowly through a hundred winding bends.
The pagoda at Hengtang seems near, yet still lies far ahead.
The river country is cold, and farm work comes late.
North of the village and south,
Only after Grain Rain are the fields all ploughed.
Wheat in ear stretches across the hills, mulberry leaves are cheap,
Soon we will taste new flour and gather fresh cocoons.

author: 王夫之

Seeking a livelihood,
I put my trust in heaven,
Not caring if earth is narrow or heaven stingy.

What difference from a floating cloud that crosses the vast sky?
In the quiet night three thousand miles of ocean waves roll,
Beneath the bright moon, I ride the staff and soar on heaven's wind.
baihua_lines: 艰难与险易原本就不放在心中，
这跟浮云飘过太空有什么区别呢？
静夜之中，海涛奔涌三万里，
明月下我执锡杖乘风飞越天风。
baihua: 艰难与险易原本就不放在心中，，这跟浮云飘过太空有什么区别呢，静夜之中，海涛奔涌三万里，，明月下我执锡杖乘风飞越天风。
en_lines: Danger and peace alike never linger in my breast,
What difference from a floating cloud that crosses the vast sky?
In the quiet night three thousand miles of ocean waves roll,
Beneath the bright moon, I ride the staff and soar on heaven's wind.

title: 七哀诗
author: 王粲
note: 【长安】汉唐都城，在今陕西西安，诗词中常借指帝都、理想之地。
【七哀诗】汉魏六朝代王粲所作的诗。
tr: 西京乱无象，豺虎方遘患。复弃中国去，委身适荆蛮。亲戚对我悲，朋友相追攀。出门无所见，白骨蔽平原。路有饥妇人，抱子弃草间。顾闻号泣声，挥涕独不还。未知身死处，何能两相完？驱马弃之去，不忍听此言。南登霸陵岸，回首望长安。悟彼下泉人，喟然伤心肝。

theme: 《七哀诗》主旨在于描绘自然山水之美，寄托隐逸或热爱自然之情。；登临怀古，借古抒怀，寄寓历史兴亡之感。作品以凝练的语言、鲜明的意象，将情感寄寓于景物与叙事之中，含蓄深沉，意蕴丰厚，千百年来引发读者广泛共鸣，是汉魏六朝代王粲的代表性作品之一。
en_body: The Western Capital lies in utter chaos,
Jackals and tigers are working their cruel will.
I must abandon the heartland of China,
And seek refuge in the southern Jing wilds.
My kinfolk face me, weeping bitterly,
My friends cling to my carriage, unwilling to part.
Once beyond the gates there is nothing to be seen,
But white bones blanketing the open plain.
By the road a starving woman stands,
Holding her child, she abandons it in the grass.
Turning back she hears its piteous wailing,
Wipes her tears and turns away again.
I know not where my own bones will be laid,
How can I hope to keep both of us alive?
I spur my horse and leave that dreadful place,
For I cannot bear to hear such words again.
Southward I climb the heights of Baling,
And turn my gaze back toward Chang'an.
I understand now the poet of the Xiaquan,
And heave a sigh that breaks my very heart.

baihua_lines: 西京长安乱得不成样子，
豺狼虎豹一般的叛贼正在制造祸乱。
我只好离开中原之地，
托身前往南方的荆蛮之地。
亲戚们对着我悲伤哭泣，
朋友们追着车拉着我依依不舍。
出门之后什么也看不见，
只见白花花的尸骨铺满了平原。
路上有一个饥饿的妇人，
抱着孩子把他丢弃在草丛之间。
回头听见孩子的号哭声，
她擦着眼泪硬是不肯回去。
自己还不知道死在哪里，
哪能两个人都保全性命呢？
我赶着马离开了那里，
实在不忍心听这样的话。
往南登上霸陵的高坡，
回头遥望着长安。
我深深体会到了《下泉》诗作者的心情，
不禁喟然叹息，心肝为之伤痛。

title: 满江红
author: 秋瑾
note: 【梦】梦境，常喻虚幻、追忆或心愿。
【满江红】明清代秋瑾所作的诗。
tr: 香雾空濛，檐牙外、流萤自照。夜向久、明河东畔，电飞云绕。错落疏星垂屋角，须臾万弩鸣林杪。渐翠竹、苍梧嫩凉生，惊秋早。人语静，签声杳。珍簟冷，纱厨小。想云窗依旧，梦寻难到。雁足空来书断绝，眉头顿著愁多少。纵细写、琴心有谁知，朱弦悄。
appr: 《满江红》是明清代秋瑾所作的诗名篇。全诗共18句，章法舒展，语言自然，情真意切。艺术上，作品善于选取典型意象融情于景，用词精炼传神，于平淡处见深情，读来余韵悠长。作为明清代诗歌的经典篇章，《满江红》历代传诵不衰，是秋瑾诗歌风格的集中体现。

en_body: Fragrant mist hangs hazy and veiled,
Beyond the eaves, fireflies glow and light their own small way.
The night wears on—east of the bright Milky Way,
Lightning flies, clouds swirl and coil.
Scattered stars hang low above the roof corners,
In an instant ten thousand crossbows hum in the treetops.
Gradually a fresh coolness stirs through green bamboo and dark parasol trees,
Startling me that autumn has arrived so soon.
Human voices fall still,
The watchman's clapper fades far away.
The precious mat is cold,
The gauze net-curtain small.
I think that cloud-window remains just as it was,
Yet even dreams can scarcely find their way there.
Wild geese come in vain, all word is broken off,
Between my brows gathers such a weight of grief.
Even if I poured my soul into the zither's strings, who would understand?
The vermeil strings are still, and no one hears.

baihua_lines: 香雾朦胧弥漫，
檐角之外，流萤闪着微光自顾照明。
夜已经深了，银河的东岸，
闪电飞驰、云彩环绕。
疏落的星星错落垂在屋角，
转眼间如万张强弩在林梢鸣响。
渐渐地翠竹、梧桐间生出阵阵嫩凉，
惊觉秋天已经早早来临。
人声静了，
竹筹报时的声音也远去了。
竹席冰凉，
纱帐窄小。
想那云窗应该依旧是原样，
梦里追寻也难以到达。
大雁空自飞来，书信已经断绝，
眉头上顿时凝聚了多少愁绪。
纵使细细把心事写进琴音，又有谁能懂，
朱红的琴弦悄然无声。

title: 黄海舟中日人索句并见日俄战争地图
author: 秋瑾
note: 【万里】极言距离之远或范围之广。
【酒】酒，古典诗词中常用于遣怀、送别、消愁。
tr: 万里乘云去复来，只身东海挟春雷。忍看图画移颜色，肯使江山付劫灰。浊酒不销忧国泪，救时应仗出群才。拼将十万头颅血，须把乾坤力挽回。
appr: 《黄海舟中日人索句并见日俄战争地图》是明清代秋瑾所作的诗名篇。全诗共八句，为律诗体裁，格律严谨、对仗工稳。首联起笔点题，颔联、颈联铺陈对仗，尾联收束点明旨意。章法井然，音韵和谐。艺术上，作品善于选取典型意象融情于景，用词精炼传神，于平淡处见深情，读来余韵悠长。作为明清代诗歌的经典篇章，《黄海舟中日人索句并见日俄战争地图》历代传诵不衰，是秋瑾诗歌风格的集中体现。
st:
【起·首联】一二句起笔点题，交代时地、情境与情感基调。
【承·颔联】三四句承接铺陈，对仗工整，拓展意境。
【转·颈联】五六句笔锋一转，由景入情或由外入内，翻出新意。
【合·尾联】七八句收束全诗，点明主旨，呼应开篇。

Why should the painted fan grieve in autumn wind?
So easily the old lover's heart has changed,
Yet you say a lover's heart is always quick to change.

Even through the Rain-Bell tears there was no resentment.

Who once swore to fly wing-to-wing, branch-to-branch?

title: 金缕曲·赠梁汾
author: 纳兰性德
note: 【酒】酒，古典诗词中常用于遣怀、送别、消愁。

tr: 德也狂生耳。偶然闻缁尘京国，乌衣门第。有酒惟浇赵州土，谁会成生此意。不信道遂成知己。青眼高歌俱未老，向尊前拭英雄泪。君不见，月如水。共君此夜须沈醉。且由倦蛾眉谣诼，古今园忌。身世悠悠何足问，冷笑置之而已。寻思起从头翻悔。一日心期千劫在，从身缘恐结他生里。然诺重，君须记。

en_body: I, De, am nothing but a reckless scholar.
By chance I found myself in the dust of the capital,
Amid these black-robed, aristocratic gates.
With wine I pour libations on the soil of Zhao,
Who could ever truly understand my heart?
Little did I think we would become sworn friends.
Black-eyed, singing loud, we are not yet old,
Before our cups we wipe the hero's burning tears.
Do you not see, my friend,
The moon is cold as water?
Tonight with you I must drink deep into drunkenness.
Let the fair-browed slander as they will,
Since ancient times envy has always been thus.
This drifting life is not worth a second thought,
I meet it with a cold laugh and nothing more.
Thinking back, I have no regrets from the start.
One day of true-hearted bond lasts through a thousand kalpas,
This life's tie may need the next life to fulfill.
A promise weighs heavy as gold,
You must keep this always in your heart.

偶然间在京城的红尘之中，

有谁能理解我这番心意。
没想到就这样与你结成了知己。
青眼高歌，我们都还未老，
在酒杯前擦干英雄的热泪。
你难道看不见，
月光凉如水。
今夜与你定要痛饮沉醉。
任凭那些蛾眉女子的造谣中伤，
自古以来就是这般招人妒忌。
身世悠悠，哪里值得挂怀，
不过冷笑一声、放在一边罢了。
回想起来，从头开始就无须后悔。
一日以心相许，历经千劫也长存，
此生的缘分恐怕还要在来生再续。
承诺重于千金，
你一定要牢记在心。
baihua: 我顾贞观不过是个狂生罢了，偶然间在京城的红尘之中，，在这乌衣门第的贵族之家，有酒就用来浇在赵州的土地上，，有谁能理解我这番心意，没想到就这样与你结成了知己，青眼高歌，我们都还未老，，在酒杯前擦干英雄的热泪，你难道看不见，，月光凉如水，今夜与你定要痛饮沉醉，任凭那些蛾眉女子的造谣中伤，，自古以来就是这般招人妒忌，身世悠悠，哪里值得挂怀，，不过冷笑一声、放在一边罢了，回想起来，从头开始就无须后悔，一日以心相许，历经千劫也长存，，此生的缘分恐怕还要在来生再续，承诺重于千金，，你一定要牢记在心。
en_lines: I, De, am nothing but a reckless scholar.
By chance I found myself in the dust of the capital,
Amid these black-robed, aristocratic gates.
With wine I pour libations on the soil of Zhao,
Who could ever truly understand my heart?
Little did I think we would become sworn friends.
Black-eyed, singing loud, we are not yet old,
Before our cups we wipe the hero's burning tears.
Do you not see, my friend,
The moon is cold as water?
Tonight with you I must drink deep into drunkenness.
Let the fair-browed slander as they will,
Since ancient times envy has always been thus.
This drifting life is not worth a second thought,
I meet it with a cold laugh and nothing more.
Thinking back, I have no regrets from the start.
One day of true-hearted bond lasts through a thousand kalpas,
This life's tie may need the next life to fulfill.
A promise weighs heavy as gold,
You must keep this always in your heart.

author: 纳兰性德
note: 【梦】梦境，常喻虚幻、追忆或心愿。

en_body: Over one mountain range,
Across one stretch of water,
I journey toward Yuguan Pass, far away,
Deep in the night, a thousand tents glow with lamps.
An hour of howling wind,
An hour of driving snow,
The clamor shatters my homesick heart, no dream can come,
For in my old home there is no such sound.

又渡过了一重水，

en_body: A mother's love for her child knows no end,
Returning home at year's end, how great her joy.
My winter coat is stitched with tight, dense thread,
The ink on recent letters from home is still fresh.
Seeing me, she pities how thin and worn I look,
Calling me close, she asks of all my hardships.
I bow my head, ashamed to be her son,
Not daring to sigh of the wind and dust of travel.

title: 满井游记
author: 袁宏道
body: 晶晶然如镜之新开而冷光之乍出于匣也。
note: 《满井游记》是袁宏道的经典作品，语言凝练，意境深远，为历代读者所传诵。【满井游记】明清代袁宏道所作的诗。

en_body: The land of Yan is cold,
After the Flower Festival,
The lingering cold is still sharp.
Freezing winds often rise,
And when they blow, sand and pebbles fly through air.
Confined within my single room,
I longed to go out but could not.
Whenever I ventured out against the wind,
Before a hundred paces I was forced to turn back.
On the twenty-second day the weather softened slightly,
I went with several friends out of Dongzhi Gate,
And arrived at Manjing, the Full Well.
Tall willows lined both sides of the embankment,
The rich soil was faintly moist,
All at once the view opened wide and empty,
And I felt like a swan just freed from its cage.
By then the icy skin of the water was just beginning to melt,
The hue of the waves was suddenly bright,
Scale-like ripples spread in layer on layer,
So clear one could see straight to the bottom,
Glistening like a mirror newly opened, a cold light flashing fresh from its case.

baihua_lines: 燕地一带天气寒冷，
花朝节过后，
余下的寒气还很厉害。
冷风时常刮起，
一刮起来就飞沙走石。
我拘束在一间小屋里面，
想要出去也出不得。
每次顶着风快步行走，
走不到百步就只能折返回来。
二十二日那天天气稍稍暖和，
我和几个朋友一起出了东直门，
来到了满井。
高高的柳树夹着堤岸，
肥沃的土地微微湿润，
一眼望去空阔辽远，
人就像从笼子里逃出来的天鹅。
这时河上的薄冰开始融化，
水波刚刚透出光亮，
鱼鳞般的浪一层一层，
清澈得可以看见水底，
亮晶晶的，就像刚打开的镜子，冷光忽然从镜匣里闪出来一般。

en_body: In the little spring, fair wind and lovely sun,
By West Lake, pavilions and terraces abound.
Those handsome and elegant young gallants,
I wonder from what place they have just come.
Imperial favor shines upon their saddled horses,
Their glory casts its glow upon the wine-cups.
If you do not seek your joy while you are here,
Who among later generations will mourn for you?

西湖边亭台池榭处处可见。

皇帝的恩光照耀着他们的鞍马，
艳丽的光彩映照着酒杯。
如今如果不及时行乐，
后人谁又会来哀怜你呢？

en_body: Elbows out, spirits high, how graceful and proud you stride,
Deep within you long to soar, and outwardly you show it.
It seems your breast has broken through the city's bustling walls,
But speak of fame and wealth, and you burn as hot as fire.
Do you know, my friend, where the ancients placed their hearts?
Listen a while—don't rush to dust your cap for office yet.
A hundred years of life flow past like a river rushing by,
What use is all this scrambling to be first, to be ahead?

en_lines: Elbows out, spirits high, how graceful and proud you stride,
Deep within you long to soar, and outwardly you show it.
It seems your breast has broken through the city's bustling walls,
But speak of fame and wealth, and you burn as hot as fire.
Do you know, my friend, where the ancients placed their hearts?
Listen a while—don't rush to dust your cap for office yet.
A hundred years of life flow past like a river rushing by,
What use is all this scrambling to be first, to be ahead?

en_body: The traces of wind and rain for years on end,
Are layered thick upon the rugged craggy stones.
Where they grow, the scene is ever still and quiet,
To look on them, all cares seem idle and at ease.
They creep on ruined walls beside the poetry pavilion,
In the herb garden they frame the empty, closed gate.
Whenever I recall the eastern path I used to walk,
I take my staff and wander slowly back alone.

en_body: Through sorrowful eyes I gaze on frost and dew,
In the cold-walled city, chrysanthemums bloom alone.
Heaven's wind follows the broken willow branches away,
A traveler's tears fall at the clear sound of border pipes.
The waters are still, the tower's shadow stretches straight,
The mountains grow dim as the frontier sun slants low.
When night falls, the homing birds have all flown off,
The last crows to roost cry out into the dark.

author: 谢朓
note: 【长安】汉唐都城，在今陕西西安，诗词中常借指帝都、理想之地。

tr: 灞涘望长安，河阳视京县。白日丽飞甍，参差皆可见。余霞散成绮，澄江静如练。喧鸟覆春洲，杂英满芳甸。去了方滞淫，怀啊罢欢宴。佳期怅何许，泪下如流霰。有情知望乡，谁能鬒不变？

en_body: From the banks of Ba I gaze back toward Chang'an,
As from Heyang men once looked toward the capital.
The white sun gilds the high-flying eaves,
Crag and rooftop, all visible stretching far and near.
The lingering clouds spread out like brocade,
The clear river lies still as a white silk cord.
Chattering birds cover the springtime islets,
Blossoms of every kind fill the fragrant meadows.
Away I must go, yet here I linger on,
Longing sorely for the feasts that now are ended.
When shall the day of my return come at last?
Tears fall down like scattered sleet across my cheeks.
All with feeling know the pain of longing for home—
Who can keep their black hair from turning white with care?

en_title: Climbing Three Mountains at Dusk and Looking Back on the Capital
baihua_lines: 我像王粲在灞陵岸回望长安一样，
像潘岳在河阳远望洛阳都城一般。
夕阳照耀着飞耸的屋檐，
高高低低都清晰可见。
天边的晚霞散开如一匹锦缎，
澄澈的江水静静得像一条白练。
喧闹的鸟儿覆盖了春天的沙洲，
各色野花开满了芬芳的郊野。
我要离开了，却又在此流连，
多么想念啊，那已经散了的欢宴。
归乡的佳期啊，何时才能到来，
眼泪像流霰一样纷纷落下。
有情人谁不懂得怀念故乡呢？
谁能受得了黑发就这样变白了？

author: 谢灵运
note: 《登池上楼》是谢灵运的经典作品，语言凝练，意境深远，为历代读者所传诵。【登池上楼】汉魏六朝代谢灵运所作的诗。

en_body: The hidden dragon delights in its quiet grace,
The soaring wild goose sends its call afar.
Gazing at the clouds, I shame before the floating bird,
Looking on the deep, I shrink before the sunken dragon.
Advancing in virtue is too clumsy for my wit,
Returning to farm, my strength is not enough.
For office I was sent to this far sea-coast,
Bedridden with illness, facing empty woods.
Beneath my quilts I lost all sense of season's change,
Then drew aside the curtains and looked out a while.
I bent my ear to listen to the waves,
And raised my eyes to gaze on the steep high hills.
The first sun of spring dispels the lingering wind,
New sunlight melts the former winter's gloom.
Spring grass is growing by the pond,
In garden willows, singing birds have changed their tune.
The Bin song of teeming plants fills me with sadness,
The Chu lament of lush green grass moves me deeply.
Living alone makes the days feel long indeed,
Cut off from friends, the heart can find no peace.
Is maintaining integrity for ancients alone?
Living without vexation—this I prove today.

en_title: Climbing the Upper Floor by the Pond
baihua_lines: 深潜的虬龙幽姿妩媚自得，
高飞的鸿雁鸣声传向远方。
仰望云霄我愧于云浮的鸿雁，
俯视深渊我怍于沉渊的潜虬。
进德修业是我智力所不能及的，
退隐躬耕我体力也担当不起。
为了俸禄我反而被贬到这偏僻的海滨，
卧病在床，空对着萧条的树林。
躺在衾枕之间不知道季节的变化，
今日我揭开帷帘，暂且登楼眺望。
侧耳倾听远处波澜的声响，
抬眼眺望巍峨高峻的山峰。
初春的阳光驱走了残余的寒风，
新的暖阳改变了冬日的阴沉。
池塘边长出了春天的青草，
园中的柳树上变换着鸣鸟的声音。
采蘩祁祁的豳歌让我伤怀，
春草生兮萋萋的楚吟让我感慨。
离群独居容易觉得日子漫长，
离开朋友就难以安心。
坚守节操难道只有古人才能做到？
遁世无闷的境界，今天就在我身上得到验证。

title: 论诗
author: 赵翼

tr: 大道本無體，何在文字間。易從先天畫，詩自聖人刪。流風傳益遠，後作莫可攀。推敲誰氏子，一字不可閑。

en_body: The great Way originally has no fixed form,
How can it reside in written words alone?
The Changes arose from the primal diagrams of old,
The Songs were winnowed and shaped by the Sage himself.
That flowing breeze has been transmitted far and wide,
No later writer has ever reached those heights.
Who is that there, weighing every word with care?
Not a single character may be idle or loose.

en_translation: The great Way originally has no fixed form,
How can it reside in written words alone?
The Changes arose from the primal diagrams of old,
The Songs were winnowed and shaped by the Sage himself.
That flowing breeze has been transmitted far and wide,
No later writer has ever reached those heights.
Who is that there, weighing every word with care?
Not a single character may be idle or loose.
baihua_lines: 大道本来没有固定的形体，
何尝只存在于文字之间。
《易经》源自先天的河图洛书，
《诗经》是由圣人孔子删定的。
流风余韵传播得越来越远，
后世作品没有人能够企及。
反复推敲的到底是谁家子弟，
每一个字都不能轻易放过。

title: 沁园春·恨
author: 郑燮
note: 【酒】酒，古典诗词中常用于遣怀、送别、消愁。
【沁园春·恨】明清代郑燮所作的诗。
tr: 花亦无知，月亦无聊，酒亦无灵。把夭桃斫断，煞他风景；鹦哥煮熟，佐我杯羹。焚砚烧书，椎琴裂画，毁尽文章抹尽名。

en_body: The flowers do not know my heart,
The moon cannot ease my weary soul,
Even wine has lost its power to console.
I would hew down the wanton peach-tree,
And spoil its pretty scene; boil the parrot,
To serve as relish with my cup of wine.
Burn the inkstone, set fire to the books,
Smash the zither, tear the paintings to shreds,
Destroy every word, wipe away every empty name.

title: 潍县署中画竹呈年伯包大中丞括
author: 郑燮
note: 【潍县署中画竹呈年伯包大中丞括】明清代郑燮所作的诗。
tr: 衙斋卧听萧萧竹，疑是民间疾苦声。些小吾曹州县吏，一枝一叶总关情。

And suspect it is the cry of folk in their suffering.
Though we are but lowly county magistrates,
Every branch and leaf tugs at our heart.

en_body: Tall bamboos cluster like canopies of green,
The great rock sits upright, square and firm.
Their steadfast joints endure the cold and still remain,
New shoots grow tall and strong as summer comes.
Clouds arise from beside the roots,
Jade is hidden within the solid trunks.
Once they follow the dragon and bring forth rain,
A pure wind fills the chrysanthemum hall.

baihua_lines: 修长的翠竹簇拥着翠旗一般的丛林，
巨大的岩石端坐其间，端庄方正。
坚劲的节操历经严寒依旧长存，
新生的竹梢入夏后蓬勃生长。

白玉一般的竹笋就藏在竹实之中。
等到化作甘霖随龙飞去之后，
清风吹满了种菊的堂前。
baihua: 修长的翠竹簇拥着翠旗一般的丛林，，巨大的岩石端坐其间，端庄方正，坚劲的节操历经严寒依旧长存，，新生的竹梢入夏后蓬勃生长，云彩从竹根上升腾而起，，白玉一般的竹笋就藏在竹实之中，等到化作甘霖随龙飞去之后，，清风吹满了种菊的堂前。
en_lines: Tall bamboos cluster like canopies of green,
The great rock sits upright, square and firm.
Their steadfast joints endure the cold and still remain,
New shoots grow tall and strong as summer comes.
Clouds arise from beside the roots,
Jade is hidden within the solid trunks.
Once they follow the dragon and bring forth rain,
A pure wind fills the chrysanthemum hall.

title: 题画兰
author: 郑燮
note: 《题画兰》是郑燮的经典作品，语言凝练，意境深远，为历代读者所传诵。【题画兰】明清代郑燮所作的诗。
tr: 向來俯首問羲皇，汝是何人到此鄉。未有畫前開鼻孔，滿天浮動古馨香。

Who are you, that have come to this far place?
Before the painting was finished, I breathed deeply in,
And all the heavens seemed filled with ancient fragrance.

title: 后秋兴
author: 钱谦益
note: 《后秋兴》是钱谦益的经典作品，语言凝练，意境深远，为历代读者所传诵。【后秋兴】明清代钱谦益所作的诗。
tr: 海角崖山一线斜，从今也不属中华。更无鱼腹捐躯地，况有龙涎泛海槎？望断关河非汉帜，吹残日月是胡笳。嫦娥老大无归处，独倚银轮哭桂花。

en_body: At the sea's edge, Mount Ya slants thin as a thread,
From this day forth it belongs no more to China.
Not even ground remains to drown oneself like Qu Yuan,
Let alone dragon-fragrance rafts to sail the seas.
Gazing out past passes and rivers, no Han flags fly,
Barbarian pipes have blown the sun and moon away.
The Moon Goddess has grown old, with no home to return,
Alone she leans on the silver wheel, weeping for the cassia.

title: 咏怀·嘉树下成蹊
author: 阮籍
note: 【秋风】秋天的风，多与萧瑟、离别、思乡相连。
【咏怀·嘉树下成蹊】汉魏六朝代阮籍所作的诗。
tr: 嘉树下成蹊，东园桃与李。秋风吹飞藿，零落从此始。繁华有憔悴，堂上生荆杞。驱马舍之去，去上西山趾。一身不自保，何况恋妻子。凝霜被野草，岁暮亦云已。
appr: 《咏怀·嘉树下成蹊》是汉魏六朝代阮籍所作的诗名篇。作品采用四言为主的句式，古朴厚重，直陈其事，是先秦古诗典型风格。艺术上，作品善于选取典型意象融情于景，用词精炼传神，于平淡处见深情，读来余韵悠长。作为汉魏六朝代诗歌的经典篇章，《咏怀·嘉树下成蹊》历代传诵不衰，是阮籍诗歌风格的集中体现。

en_body: Beneath fine trees a path is trod by many feet,
So it is with the peach and plum in the eastern garden.
Autumn winds blow the bean-leaves flying about,
And the withering and falling begins from this hour.
All prosperity must one day fade and languish,
Thorns and brambles will grow in the hall itself.
I whip my horse, abandon this place and go,
To make my home at the western mountain's foot.
Even my own single self I cannot keep safe,
Let alone clinging to wife and children dear.
Heavy frost covers the wild grasses of the field,
As the year draws to an end, all things come to a close.

baihua_lines: 美好的树下自然会被人踩出小路，
那就是东园里的桃树和李树。
秋风吹起，豆叶纷纷飘落，
草木的零落从此就开始了。
繁华总有凋零憔悴的一天，
殿堂之上也会长出荆杞野草。
我赶着马舍弃这里离开，
要去那西山脚下隐居。
自身都尚且不能保全，
更何况还贪恋妻子儿女。
浓霜覆盖了野外的百草，
岁暮之时，一切也就这样完结了。
baihua: 美好的树下自然会被人踩出小路，，那就是东园里的桃树和李树，秋风吹起，豆叶纷纷飘落，，草木的零落从此就开始了，繁华总有凋零憔悴的一天，，殿堂之上也会长出荆杞野草，我赶着马舍弃这里离开，，要去那西山脚下隐居，自身都尚且不能保全，，更何况还贪恋妻子儿女，浓霜覆盖了野外的百草，，岁暮之时，一切也就这样完结了。
en_lines: Beneath fine trees a path is trod by many feet,
So it is with the peach and plum in the eastern garden.
Autumn winds blow the bean-leaves flying about,
And the withering and falling begins from this hour.
All prosperity must one day fade and languish,
Thorns and brambles will grow in the hall itself.
I whip my horse, abandon this place and go,
To make my home at the western mountain's foot.
Even my own single self I cannot keep safe,
Let alone clinging to wife and children dear.
Heavy frost covers the wild grasses of the field,
As the year draws to an end, all things come to a close.

author: 阮籍
note: 【明月】皎洁的月亮，古典诗词中常寄托思乡、怀人之情。

en_body: In the middle of the night I cannot sleep,
I sit up and start to pluck the singing zither.
Through thin curtains the bright moon casts its light,
A clear wind gently flutters at my robe.
A lonely wild goose cries out across the wilds,
A circling bird calls in the northern grove.
I pace back and forth—what is there to be seen?
Only sorrowful thoughts, that wound my heart alone.

title: 点绛唇·春日风雨有感
author: 陈子龙
note: 【相思】彼此思念，多指男女之间或友人之间的深切思念。

en_body: As far as the eye can see, spring's splendor blooms,
Yet the east wind is wont to blow the red flowers away.
Time and again the mist and rain descend,
And flowers alone are impossible to save.
In dreams my longing travels,
Along the road the prince took to his fallen kingdom.
Spring has no master now!
Where the cuckoo cries its tears of blood,
My own tears fall through rouge-red rain.

title: 饮马长城窟行
author: 陈琳
note: 【千里】形容路途遥远。
【饮马长城窟行】汉魏六朝代陈琳所作的诗。
tr: 長安少年無遠圖，一生惟羨執金吾。麒麟前殿拜天子，走馬西擊長城胡。胡沙獵獵吹人面，漢虜相逢不相見。遙聞鼙鼓動地來，傳道單于夜猶戰。此時顧恩寧顧身，爲君一行摧萬人。壯士揮戈迴白日，單于濺血染朱輪。歸來飲馬長城窟，長城道傍多白骨。問之耆老何代人，云是秦王築城卒。黃昏塞北無人煙，鬼哭啾啾聲沸天。無罪見誅功不賞，孤魂流落此城邊。當昔秦王按劒起，諸侯膝行不敢視。富國强兵二十年，築怨興徭九千里。秦王築城何太愚，天實亡秦非北胡。一朝禍起蕭墻內，渭水咸陽不復都。

en_body: The young men of Chang'an have no grand designs,
All their lives they envy only the Imperial Guard.
Before the Unicorn Hall they bow before the Emperor,
Then ride west to strike the Hu beyond the Wall.
The desert wind of Hu blows sharp against their faces,
Han and Hu draw near, yet never truly meet.
From far off comes the thunder of war drums shaking earth,
Word passes that the Chanyu still fights through the night.
In this hour, remembering grace, who cares for his own life?
For the sovereign, one charge shatters ten thousand men.
Brave warriors swing their spears to turn back the very sun,
The Chanyu's blood splatters red upon the crimson wheels.
Returning, they water their horses at the Great Wall springs,
Beside the long road, white bones lie strewn in piles.
Asking the old men: what age saw these men perish?
They say these were the laborers who built the Wall for Qin.
At dusk, beyond the Wall no smoke of hearth-fire rises,
Ghosts wail and shriek, their cries rising to heaven.
Slaughtered without guilt, their deeds rewarded with nothing,
Their lonely souls wander drifting by the city wall.
In those days the First Emperor rose, hand on his sword,
Feudal lords crawled on their knees, not daring to look up.
Twenty years he spent enriching state and strengthening arms,
Building resentment and corvée across nine thousand li.
How foolish was the First Emperor building that Wall,
For Heaven doomed Qin—not the Hu of the north.
One morning calamity arose from within the very palace walls,
And Xianyang by the Wei became a capital no more.

en_translation: The young men of Chang'an have no grand designs,
All their lives they envy only the Imperial Guard.
Before the Unicorn Hall they bow before the Emperor,
Then ride west to strike the Hu beyond the Wall.
The desert wind of Hu blows sharp against their faces,
Han and Hu draw near, yet never truly meet.
From far off comes the thunder of war drums shaking earth,
Word passes that the Chanyu still fights through the night.
In this hour, remembering grace, who cares for his own life?
For the sovereign, one charge shatters ten thousand men.
Brave warriors swing their spears to turn back the very sun,
The Chanyu's blood splatters red upon the crimson wheels.
Returning, they water their horses at the Great Wall springs,
Beside the long road, white bones lie strewn in piles.
Asking the old men: what age saw these men perish?
They say these were the laborers who built the Wall for Qin.
At dusk, beyond the Wall no smoke of hearth-fire rises,
Ghosts wail and shriek, their cries rising to heaven.
Slaughtered without guilt, their deeds rewarded with nothing,
Their lonely souls wander drifting by the city wall.
In those days the First Emperor rose, hand on his sword,
Feudal lords crawled on their knees, not daring to look up.
Twenty years he spent enriching state and strengthening arms,
Building resentment and corvée across nine thousand li.
How foolish was the First Emperor building that Wall,
For Heaven doomed Qin—not the Hu of the north.
One morning calamity arose from within the very palace walls,
And Xianyang by the Wei became a capital no more.
en_title: Watering Horses at the Great Wall Spring
baihua_lines: 长安的少年没有远大的图谋，
一辈子只羡慕做个执金吾的武官。
在麒麟前殿拜见了天子，
就骑马西征，去攻打长城外的胡人。
胡地的风沙猎猎地吹着脸面，
汉军与胡人相遇，却不能真正相见。
远远听见战鼓震天动地而来，
传说单于夜里还在激战。
这时候想着皇恩，哪里还顾惜自身，
为君王一去就可摧破万人。
壮士挥动长戈，能把白日挽回，
单于的鲜血染红了朱红的车轮。
归来之后在长城泉窟饮马，
长城的路旁白骨累累。
询问老人：这些是什么年代的人，
说都是秦王当年筑长城的兵卒。
黄昏时节塞北荒无人烟，
鬼哭声啾啾，声音响彻云天。
无罪被杀、有功不赏，
孤魂流落徘徊在这座城边。
想当年秦始皇按着宝剑起身，
诸侯们膝行而前，不敢抬头仰视。
富国强兵用了二十年的经营，
结下怨恨、征发徭役长达九千里。
秦王筑长城真是太愚昧了，
其实是上天要亡秦，并不是北方胡人的缘故。
有朝一日祸乱从内部萧墙兴起，
渭水边的咸阳城再也做不成都城了。

title: 五柳先生传
author: 陶渊明
body: 或置酒而招之；造饮辄尽，
赞曰：黔娄之妻有言：不戚戚于贫贱，
note: 【酒】酒，古典诗词中常用于遣怀、送别、消愁。
【五柳先生传】汉魏六朝代陶渊明所作的诗。
tr: 先生不知何许人也，亦不详其姓字，宅边有五柳树，因以为号焉。闲静少言，不慕荣利。好读书，不求甚解；每有会意，便欣然忘食。性嗜酒，家贫不能常得。亲旧知其如此，或置酒而招之；造饮辄尽，期在必醉。既醉而退，曾不吝情去留。环堵萧然，不蔽风日；短褐穿结，箪瓢屡空，晏如也。常著文章自娱，颇示己志。忘怀得失，以此自终。赞曰：黔娄之妻有言：不戚戚于贫贱，不汲汲于富贵。其言兹若人之俦乎？衔觞赋诗，以乐其志。无怀氏之民欤？葛天氏之民欤？

theme: 《五柳先生传》主旨在于登临怀古，借古抒怀，寄寓历史兴亡之感。；表达喜悦、欢畅或旷达之情。作品以凝练的语言、鲜明的意象，将情感寄寓于景物与叙事之中，含蓄深沉，意蕴丰厚，千百年来引发读者广泛共鸣，是汉魏六朝代陶渊明的代表性作品之一。
en_body: The Master is not known from what place he came,
Nor are his name and courtesy-name clearly known,
But beside his cottage grew five willow trees,
And so he took 'Five Willows' as his style.
He was quiet and still, speaking but few words,
And did not chase after glory or gain.
He loved to read books,
Without seeking overly subtle explanations; whenever something struck his heart,
He was so overjoyed he forgot to eat.
By nature he was exceedingly fond of wine,
But his household was poor and could not always afford it.
Relatives and old friends knowing this of him,
Sometimes prepared wine and invited him over; he would go and drink to his fill,
Intent on becoming thoroughly drunk.
Once drunk he would take his leave and go home,
With no hesitation about staying or leaving.
Within his bare walls all was empty and bare,
Not enough to shelter from wind and sun; his short coarse coat was patched and worn,
His rice basket and ladle were often empty,
Yet he remained perfectly at peace.
He often wrote literary pieces to amuse himself,
Which amply revealed the bent of his heart.
He forgot all thoughts of gain and loss,
And in this way he lived out all his days.
Appraisal: Qian Lou's wife once said: 'Do not grieve over poverty and low station,
Do not chase anxiously after wealth and high rank.'
Do these words not describe just such a man as this?
Drinking wine and chanting poems,
He gladdened his heart by such pursuits.
Was he not a subject of the Age of Wuhuai?
Or perhaps a subject of the Age of Getian?

一边饮酒一边赋诗，

title: 归去来兮辞
author: 陶渊明
body: 归去来兮，田园将芜胡不归？
归去来兮，请息交以绝游。
世与我而相违，复驾言兮焉求？
note: 【兮】楚辞及古诗常见语气词，相当于"啊"，用于舒缓节奏、增强咏叹意味。
【酒】酒，古典诗词中常用于遣怀、送别、消愁。
tr: 归去来啊，田园将芜胡不归？既自以心为形役，奚惆怅而独悲？悟已往之不谏，知来者之可追。实迷途其未远，觉今是而昨非。舟遥遥以轻飏，风飘飘而吹衣。问征夫以前路，恨晨光之熹微。乃瞻衡宇，载欣载奔。僮仆欢迎，稚子候门。三径就荒，松菊犹存。携幼入室，有酒盈樽。引壶觞以自酌，眄庭柯以怡颜。倚南窗以寄傲，审容膝之易安。园日涉以成趣，门虽设而常关。策扶老以流憩，时矫首而遐观。云无心以出岫，鸟倦飞而知还。景翳翳以将入，抚孤松而盘桓。归去来啊，请息交以绝游。世与我而相违，复驾言啊，焉求？悦亲戚之情话，乐琴书以消忧。农人告余以春及，将有事于西畴。或命巾车，或棹孤舟。既窈窕以寻壑，亦崎岖而经丘。木欣欣以向荣，泉涓涓而始流。善万物之得时，感吾生之行休。已了乎！寓形宇内复几时？曷不委心任去留？胡为乎遑遑欲何之？富贵非吾愿，帝乡不可期。怀良辰以孤往，或植杖而耘耔。登东皋以舒啸，临清流而赋诗。聊乘化以归尽，乐夫天命复奚疑！

theme: 《归去来兮辞》主旨在于抒写羁旅思乡之情，表达对故土亲人的深切思念。；表现边塞征戍之苦与家国豪情。作品以凝练的语言、鲜明的意象，将情感寄寓于景物与叙事之中，含蓄深沉，意蕴丰厚，千百年来引发读者广泛共鸣，是汉魏六朝代陶渊明的代表性作品之一。
en_body: Come away home! The fields and gardens will run to waste—why not return?
Since I allowed my heart to be enslaved by my body,
Why bow myself down with lonely grief and melancholy?
I know that what is past cannot be mended,
But what is yet to come I may still overtake.
Indeed I have not wandered far astray,
And I see clearly that today I am right, and yesterday I was wrong.
My boat rocks lightly, drifting on the water,
The wind blows softly, fluttering my gown.
I ask a traveler how much farther lies ahead,
Resenting that the morning light is still so dim.
At last I catch sight of my humble thatched roof,
With joyful heart I hurry forward, running.
My servants greet me with happy welcome,
My youngest child waits by the door.
The three paths to the door are almost overgrown,
But the pines and chrysanthemums still stand there.
Leading the little one by the hand I enter the house,
Where wine already fills the goblet to the brim.
I lift the pot and pour myself a drink,
Gaze at the courtyard trees, and a smile comes to my face.
Leaning against the southern window I nurse my proud resolve,
Knowing how easy it is to find peace in so small a room.
Daily I walk the garden, and my pleasure grows,
Though there is a gate, it mostly remains shut.
Staff in hand I wander and rest at will,
Now and then lifting my head to gaze afar.
Clouds drift aimless from out the mountain caves,
Birds, tired of flight, know well when to return.
The light grows dim as the sun begins to set,
I caress the lonely pine and linger, loath to leave.
Come away home! Let me sever all social ties and roam no more.
Since the world and I have fallen out, why drive forth seeking anything?
The loving chatter of kinsfolk brings joy to the heart,
Playing the zither and reading books dissolves all care.
The farmers tell me spring is here at last,
There will be work to do in the western fields.
Sometimes I call for a covered cart,
Sometimes I row a solitary boat.
Winding through narrow chasms I explore the valleys deep,
Or follow rugged paths across the rolling hills.
The trees burgeon forth in glorious thriving life,
The spring water trickles, beginning its flow.
I rejoice that all living things meet their due season,
And feel that my own life is drawing to its close.
Enough, then, I say!
How long will this body abide within the universe?
Why not set the heart free, let it go or stay as it will?
Why all this anxious hurry, and to where?
Wealth and high office are not my desire,
The immortal realms are beyond my hoping.
I will cherish fair days and go wandering alone,
Or plant my staff and go weeding and hoeing the fields.
I will climb the eastern marsh and whistle long,
Or stand by a clear stream and recite my poems.
Let me ride with the Transformation till I return to the end,
Content with Heaven's will—what doubts can trouble me then?

lines: 归去来兮，田园将芜胡不归？
归去来兮，请息交以绝游。
世与我而相违，复驾言兮焉求？
baihua_lines: 回去吧！田园快要荒芜了，为什么还不回去呢？
既然自己让心灵被形体所驱使奴役，
为什么还要惆怅、独自伤悲呢？
我明白过去的已经不可挽回，
知道未来的岁月还来得及补救。
确实是走入迷途还不算太远，
我已经觉悟到今天做对了，而从前是错的。
小船在水面上轻轻飘荡，
微风飘飘吹拂着我的衣裳。
向行人打听前面的路程，
只恨晨光还那样朦胧微弱。
终于看见了自家的茅屋，
我心中欣喜，奔跑过去。
仆人们欢欢喜喜出来迎接，
小儿子在门口等候。
院子里的小路快要荒芜了，
松树和菊花还依然挺立着。
我拉着小儿子走进屋里，
屋里美酒已经斟满了酒杯。
拿起酒壶酒杯自斟自饮，
看着院子里的树木，脸上露出了笑容。
靠着南窗来寄托自己傲世的情怀，
深知这狭小的居所反而容易让人安心。
每天在园子里散步，趣味无穷，
虽然有门，却常常是关着的。
拄着拐杖四处游憩，
不时抬头眺望远天。
白云自然而然地从山穴中飘出，
鸟儿飞累了也知道回巢。
日光暗淡，太阳即将落山，
我抚摸着孤松，流连忘返。
回去吧！让我断绝与世俗的交游。
世事与我的心意相违背，我还驾车出去追求什么呢？
与亲戚们说说知心话叫人心情愉悦，
弹琴读书足以消解忧愁。
农人告诉我春天已经到了，
就要到西边的田里去春耕了。
有时驾着有帷幕的小车，
有时划着一叶孤舟。
既循着幽深曲折的溪水去寻访山谷，
也沿着崎岖不平的小路走过山丘。
树木生机勃勃，欣欣向荣，
泉水涓涓地开始流淌。
我羡慕万物正得其时，生机勃勃，
感叹我的一生即将走到尽头。
算了吧！
寄身于天地之间还能有多少日子呢？
为什么不放下心来顺其自然地面对生死去留？
为什么遑遑不安，想要去哪里呢？
富贵不是我的愿望，
修仙成神也没有期望。
爱惜这美好的时光，独自出去游玩，
或者把手杖插在一旁，去田里除草培苗。
登上东边的高岗放声长啸，
面对清澈的流水吟诵诗篇。
姑且顺着造化走向生命的尽头，
乐天安命，还有什么可怀疑的呢！

title: 归园田居·其一
author: 陶渊明
note: 【归园田居·其一】汉魏六朝代陶渊明所作的诗。
tr: 少无适俗韵，性本爱丘山。误落尘网中，一去三十年。羁鸟恋旧林，池鱼思故渊。开荒南野际，守拙归园田。方宅十余亩，草屋八九间。榆柳荫后檐，桃李罗堂前。暧暧远人村，依依墟里烟。狗吠深巷中，鸡鸣桑树颠。户庭无尘杂，虚室有余闲。久在樊笼里，复得返自然。

en_body: From my youth I had no taste for worldly airs,
By nature I loved only hills and mountains.
By mistake I fell into the dust's net,
And there I stayed for thirty years gone by.
A caged bird longs for its old familiar woods,
A fish in a pond dreams of its former deep pool.
I cleared new ground by the edge of southern wilds,
And keeping to my simple ways returned to field and garden.
My holding is little more than ten acres,
With eight or nine rough-thatched rooms.
Elms and willows shade the back eaves,
Peach and plum are arrayed before the hall.
Distant villages faint and blur in sight,
Village smoke curls gently up into the air.
A dog barks deep within a narrow lane,
A rooster crows from the top of a mulberry tree.
My door and courtyard know no worldly din,
My empty rooms abound with quiet leisure.
So long was I caged in a narrow pen,
Now I have returned again to Nature.

en_title: Returning to Live in Fields and Gardens: I
baihua_lines: 年少时就没有迎合世俗的气质，
天性本来就热爱山川自然。
错误地落入了尘世的罗网之中，
一去就是整整三十年。
笼中的鸟儿思念旧日的树林，
池中的鱼儿思念从前的深潭。
我到南边的田野里开荒垦地，
固守着愚拙的心，回到田园中来。
宅子周围有十余亩地，
草屋有那么八九间。
榆树柳树荫蔽着后檐，
桃树李树罗列在堂屋前面。
远处的村庄若隐若现，
村里的炊烟袅袅升起。
狗在深巷里吠叫，
鸡在桑树的顶端啼鸣。
门庭里没有尘俗的杂事，
静室里多的是悠闲的时光。
长久地被关在樊笼里，
如今终于能够重返大自然了。

title: 归园田居·其三
author: 陶渊明
note: 【归园田居·其三】汉魏六朝代陶渊明所作的诗。
tr: 种豆南山下，草盛豆苗稀。晨兴理荒秽，带月荷锄归。道狭草木长，夕露沾我衣。衣沾不足惜，但使愿无违。

en_body: I planted beans beneath the southern hills,
Weeds grew thick, but the bean sprouts came up thin.
I rose at dawn to clear the weeds away,
Shouldering my hoe, I returned when the moon rose high.
The path was narrow, overgrown with grass and trees,
The evening dew fell and soaked my clothes through.
Wet clothes are not a thing worth grieving over,
So long as I do not betray my heart's true wish.

en_title: Returning to Live in Fields and Gardens: III
baihua_lines: 在南山下种豆子，
野草茂盛，豆苗却稀稀疏疏。
清晨起来就下地铲除杂草，
直到月亮升起才扛着锄头回家。
道路狭窄，草木丛生，
傍晚的露水打湿了我的衣裳。
衣裳打湿了并不值得可惜，
只要不违背我归隐的心愿就好。

title: 杂诗·人生无根蒂
author: 陶渊明
note: 【酒】酒，古典诗词中常用于遣怀、送别、消愁。

en_body: Human life has no root or anchorage,
It drifts like the dust upon the road.
Blown by winds it scatters, turns and shifts,
And this same body is never what it was.
Born into this world, we should be brothers all,
Why must only blood kin count as one's own?
When joy is found, let us seize it and be merry,
With wine call in the neighbors and drink together.
Our prime years come not back a second time,
No morning ever rises twice in one day.
We must urge ourselves on while still strong in years,
For the months and years wait for no man.

en_translation: Human life has no root or anchorage,
It drifts like the dust upon the road.
Blown by winds it scatters, turns and shifts,
And this same body is never what it was.
Born into this world, we should be brothers all,
Why must only blood kin count as one's own?
When joy is found, let us seize it and be merry,
With wine call in the neighbors and drink together.
Our prime years come not back a second time,
No morning ever rises twice in one day.
We must urge ourselves on while still strong in years,
For the months and years wait for no man.
en_title: Miscellaneous Poem: Human Life Has No Root
baihua_lines: 人生在世没有根蒂，
漂泊不定就像路上的尘土。
生命随风飘散、辗转迁徙，
此身早已不是原来的样子了。
落地降生就应该成为兄弟，
何必非要骨肉至亲才算亲人！
遇到高兴的事就应当及时作乐，
有酒就邀请邻居一起来聚饮。
青春年华一旦过去就不会重来，
一天之内不会有第二个早晨。
应当趁年富力强之时勉励自己，
岁月是不会等待任何人的。

title: 桃花源记
author: 陶渊明
body: 此中人语云：不足为外人道也。
note: 【酒】酒，古典诗词中常用于遣怀、送别、消愁。
【桃花源记】汉魏六朝代陶渊明所作的诗。
tr: 晋太元中，武陵人捕鱼为业。缘溪行，忘路之远近。忽逢桃花林，夹岸数百步，中无杂树，芳草鲜美，落英缤纷。渔人甚异之，复前行，欲穷其林。林尽水源，便得一山，山有小口，仿佛若有光。便舍船，从口入。初极狭，才通人。复行数十步，豁然开朗。土地平旷，屋舍俨然，有良田、美池、桑竹之属。阡陌交通，鸡犬相闻。其中往来种作，男女衣着，悉如外人。黄发垂髫，并怡然自乐。见渔人，乃大惊，问所从来。具答之。便要还家，设酒杀鸡作食。村中闻有此人，咸来问讯。自云先世避秦时乱，率妻子邑人来此绝境，不复出焉，遂与外人间隔。问今是何世，乃不知有汉，无论魏晋。此人一一为具言所闻，皆叹惋。余人各复延至其家，皆出酒食。停数日，辞去。此中人语云：不足为外人道也。既出，得其船，便扶向路，处处志之。及郡下，诣太守，说如此。太守即遣人随其往，寻向所志，遂迷，不复得路。南阳刘子骥，高尚士也，闻之，欣然规往。未果，寻病终。后遂无问津者。

en_body: During the Taiyuan period of the Jin dynasty,
There lived in Wuling a man who made his living fishing.
One day as he rowed along a stream,
He forgot how far he had traveled.
Suddenly he came upon a grove of peach trees in bloom,
Stretching for several hundred paces along both banks,
Among which grew no other kind of tree,
And fragrant grass grew fresh and beautiful,
While fallen blossoms scattered in profusion.
The fisherman was greatly astonished at this sight,
And he continued rowing forward,
Intent on reaching the end of the grove.
Where the peach grove ended, at the stream's source,
There rose a mountain,
And in the mountain was a small opening,
From which there seemed to glow a faint light.
The fisherman thereupon left his boat,
And entered through the opening.
At first it was extremely narrow,
Barely wide enough for one person to pass.
After walking another several dozen paces,
Suddenly the view opened out into wide clear space.
He saw flat and spacious land,
Houses laid out neatly in order,
With fertile fields, beautiful ponds, mulberry and bamboo and the like.
Paths between the fields ran crisscross,
And the crowing of roosters and barking of dogs could be heard all around.
People there were coming and going, working in the fields,
The clothes worn by men and women alike
Were exactly like those of people outside.
The old people with yellow hair and the young children with hanging locks
Were all happy and contented.
When the people of the place saw the fisherman,
They were greatly startled,
And asked him where he had come from.
The fisherman answered all their questions in detail.
They then invited him to their homes,
Setting out wine, killing chickens, preparing meals to entertain him.
When others in the village heard of this stranger,
They all came to ask for news.
They told how their ancestors, fleeing the wars of the Qin dynasty,
Had led their wives, children and fellow villagers to this isolated land,
And never again ventured out,
Thereby cutting themselves off from the world outside.
They asked what dynasty reigned at present,
Not knowing that the Han dynasty had ever existed,
Let alone the Wei and the Jin.
The fisherman told them in great detail all he knew,
At which they all sighed in wonder and regret.
Others in turn invited him to their own homes,
And all set out wine and food to entertain him.
After staying several days,
The fisherman took his leave and departed.
The people there told him: This place is not worth speaking of to those outside.
Once the fisherman had come out,
He found his boat again,
And followed the route by which he had come,
Making marks all along the way.
When he reached the commandery city of Wuling,
He went to call on the governor,
And told him of this discovery.
The governor immediately sent men to go with him,
To search for the marks he had made,
But they lost their way,
And could never find the road to Peach Blossom Spring again.
A gentleman of Nanyang named Liu Ziji,
Was a scholar of noble, hermit-like character;
Hearing of this,
He gladly made plans to go and search for it.
But his plan came to nothing,
And before long he fell ill and died.
After that, no one ever went to seek the spring again.

lines: 此中人语云：不足为外人道也。
baihua_lines: 晋朝太元年间，
武陵有个人以打鱼为生。
一天他沿着溪水划船，
忘记了路程有多远。
忽然遇到一片桃花林，
溪流两岸几百步之内，
中间没有别的杂树，
地上的芳草鲜嫩美丽，
坠落的花瓣纷繁杂乱。
渔人对此感到非常惊讶，
又继续往前划行，
想走到林子的尽头。
桃林的尽头正是溪水的源头，
在那里看到一座山，
山上有个小洞口，
里面隐隐约约好像有光。
渔人就丢下了船，
从洞口走进去。
起初洞口非常狭窄，
只能容一个人通过。
又走了几十步，
眼前突然变得开阔敞亮。
只见土地平坦宽广，
房屋整整齐齐，
还有肥沃的田地、美丽的池塘、桑树竹子之类。
田间小路交错相通，
鸡鸣狗叫彼此都能听见。
那里面的人们来来往往耕种劳作，
男女穿的衣服，
都和外面的人一模一样。
老人和小孩，
都安闲快乐。
村里的人看见了渔人，
于是大吃一惊，
问他是从哪里来的。
渔人详细地回答了他们。
村里人就邀请他到家里去，
备酒、杀鸡、做饭来款待他。
村里的人听说来了这么一个人，
都来打听消息。
他们自己说祖先为了躲避秦朝的战乱，
领着妻子儿女和同乡人来到这个与世隔绝的地方，
从此以后就不再出去，
于是就和外面的人断绝了往来。
他们问现在是什么朝代，
竟然不知道有过汉朝，
更不用说魏朝和晋朝了。
这个渔人把自己知道的一一详细地告诉了他们，
他们听了都感叹惋惜。
其余的人又各自把渔人请到自己家中，
都拿出酒饭来招待他。
渔人停留了几天，
就告辞离开了。
这里面的人嘱咐他说：这里的情况不值得对外面的人说啊。
渔人出来以后，
找到了他的船，
就沿着来时的路往回走，
处处都做了标记。
到了郡城武陵，
渔人去拜见了太守，
禀报了这件事。
太守立即派人跟着他前去，
寻找之前做的标记，
结果却迷了路，
再也找不到通往桃花源的路了。
南阳人刘子骥，
是一位志向高洁的隐士，
听说了这件事，
高高兴兴地计划前去寻找。
但没有实现，
不久就因病去世了。
后来就再也没有人去探寻桃花源了。

The fisherman was greatly astonished at this sight,
And he continued rowing forward,
Intent on reaching the end of the grove.
Where the peach grove ended, at the stream's source,
There rose a mountain,
And in the mountain was a small opening,
From which there seemed to glow a faint light.
The fisherman thereupon left his boat,
And entered through the opening.
At first it was extremely narrow,
Barely wide enough for one person to pass.
After walking another several dozen paces,
Suddenly the view opened out into wide clear space.
He saw flat and spacious land,
Houses laid out neatly in order,
With fertile fields, beautiful ponds, mulberry and bamboo and the like.
Paths between the fields ran crisscross,
And the crowing of roosters and barking of dogs could be heard all around.
People there were coming and going, working in the fields,
The clothes worn by men and women alike
Were exactly like those of people outside.
The old people with yellow hair and the young children with hanging locks
Were all happy and contented.
When the people of the place saw the fisherman,
They were greatly startled,
And asked him where he had come from.
The fisherman answered all their questions in detail.
They then invited him to their homes,
Setting out wine, killing chickens, preparing meals to entertain him.
When others in the village heard of this stranger,
They all came to ask for news.
They told how their ancestors, fleeing the wars of the Qin dynasty,
Had led their wives, children and fellow villagers to this isolated land,
And never again ventured out,
Thereby cutting themselves off from the world outside.
They asked what dynasty reigned at present,
Not knowing that the Han dynasty had ever existed,
Let alone the Wei and the Jin.
The fisherman told them in great detail all he knew,
At which they all sighed in wonder and regret.
Others in turn invited him to their own homes,
And all set out wine and food to entertain him.
After staying several days,
The fisherman took his leave and departed.
The people there told him: This place is not worth speaking of to those outside.
Once the fisherman had come out,
He found his boat again,
And followed the route by which he had come,
Making marks all along the way.
When he reached the commandery city of Wuling,
He went to call on the governor,
And told him of this discovery.
The governor immediately sent men to go with him,
To search for the marks he had made,
But they lost their way,
And could never find the road to Peach Blossom Spring again.
A gentleman of Nanyang named Liu Ziji,
Was a scholar of noble, hermit-like character;
Hearing of this,
He gladly made plans to go and search for it.
But his plan came to nothing,
And before long he fell ill and died.
After that, no one ever went to seek the spring again.
